papers.text: A motorway bench for watching coaches go by. Where the hedge is now.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Put the National Clock back an hour on show day. Growers need more time.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Light the harbour wall like a shop window. Anglers to sit tastefully.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: May the Society have your second telephone? The League rings it 40 times a day.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A bandstand on wheels, to follow the audience. It is at the kites.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Give the marrows the band's Sunday. They have a performing licence.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Tune the foghorn to B flat. Then the next one to F. Then book a fog.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Till's Teas will sponsor the lamps, if they glow the colour of tea. Milky.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Wave at the 6:15 coach for the Society's album. It has never waved back.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A sign in the arcade: PRIZE PUMPKIN, THIS WAY. It points outside.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Sunday practice on the motorway footbridge. The rare coaches run on Sundays.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A spotting platform by the motorway. The bank is 80 % onion bed.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Give the League the harbour wall. Anglers may apply to sit on the water.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Soundproof the band's end of the harbour. Then the middle. Then the band.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Hold the hedge show on the kite field. Any kite that lands gets clipped.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Hear the band down your third telephone, for the camera. Nod in time.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A meter on our lake, to count the growers' watering cans. By hand.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Signs on the lamp posts: KITES MAY REST HERE. The Guild's baskets to budge up.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Clip the arcade hedge into a shop window. Then a hat for it. Then a shopper.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Dim the Guild's harbour windows at dusk. The water is 40 % hat.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The band will hire a lighthouse for one concert. The tunes go round.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Unhook your telephones for the Quiet Competition. Till's Teas will keep trying.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will pay for a hedge down the middle of the motorway. Spotters lose the far side.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Walk the arcade with the band, carrying the cymbals. Carrying only.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A landing circle by the marrow beds. Kites miss circles by 3 metres.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will pay to name a motorway junction after the pumpkin. Then the rest.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Launch a kite named after you. Smile before it finds the hedge.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: The Circle will sponsor the National Clock's quietest minute. Plaque: SHH.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: A working group on whether a coach seen in a shop window counts as seen.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The group now asks whether a coach seen in a puddle counts. It needs a wet year.

papers.text: Your face on the National Clock. At noon, both hands will point at you.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study of marrows by lamplight. Half the lamps go off, as a control.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The marrow study asks for a second control: the other half of the lamps.

papers.text: A desk lamp, as a gift. It glows near scissors. Any openings? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the lamp: it would like a solo at the Sunday concert. It glows.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S LAMP GIVEN SOLO; BAND PLAYS IN THE DARK
clippings.refuse: LAMP STAYS ON THE DESK, GLOWING AT NOTHING

papers.text: Light the hedge show on the kite field. Stand by the switch, looking pleased.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A working group on dressing the lighthouse window. Every idea is Till's Teas.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The lighthouse group now wishes to dress the beam. Stripes, on alternate sweeps.

papers.text: A lighthouse that flashes your initials. Then your name. Then your speeches.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A working group on whether a humming kite is an instrument. Bring kites.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The group asks to study a whistling kite as well, and one that sighs.

papers.text: A plaque on every lamp: LIT BY THE PRESIDENT. I have done four so far.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A working group on the anglers' willow: is it a hedge? If so, it gets trimmed.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The willow group asks to inspect every willow in the Republic. Shears packed.

papers.text: Three small umbrellas, one per telephone. Do say 'rain' when you answer?
papers.subject: vanity

favour.text: About the umbrellas: they would like to judge the marrow show. Open.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S UMBRELLA JUDGES MARROWS; GROWERS DAMP
clippings.refuse: UMBRELLAS STAY BY THE TELEPHONES, OPINIONS UNSHARED

papers.text: A study of which awnings kites land on. So far, 9 in 10 prefer stripes.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The awning study asks to study plain awnings too, for balance. And spots.
